item.title: Healthy Church: The Goal
item.description:
Healthy Church: The Goal

Titus 1

Series: Healthy Church: Paul's Letter to Titus

Preacher: Richard Glover

What makes a church good?

Or, to use the language of the letter to Titus: What makes a church healthy?

In Paul's letter to Titus, we discover what makes a church healthy. A healthy church is one that makes Christians, grows Christians, and helps them to stay Christians. Titus is given the daunting task of establishing healthy churches in the company of gangsters: Crete in the time this letter was written was much like 'Razorhurst'—the nickname affectionately (?!) given to Darlinghurst and Kings Cross in the 1930s and 1940s heyday of organised crime. 

What would Titus need to establish healthy churches in a place like that? He must hold fast to the truth, which will bring about renewal in godliness, and issue forth in meaningful speech.

And all that makes for a healthy church is applied to a particular sphere of church life: pastoral leadership. 

Sermon text: Titus 1

item.title: Washed: A Sermon on Baptism
item.description:
Washed: A Sermon on Baptism

Romans 6.1–14; 1 Peter 3.18–22

Preacher: Richard Glover

What are we doing when we baptise? What's it about, how does it work, and what does it do? 

Baptism is a "visible word" from God to us. It refers to our washing, our clean conscience before God, through the death and resurrection of Jesus. It assures us that we really are clean; it encourages us to persevere in free, holy living; it defines us as a community of welcome; and sends us on mission. 

On a Sunday when we witnessed the baptisms of a child and an adult, we take some time to reflect on the gift of baptism.
